option_description: Attestation that the broker's shipped default accounts (e.g. RabbitMQ guest:guest, vendor-default Kafka/ActiveMQ principals) have been deleted or re-credentialed rather than left usable.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Default / anonymous / weak broker authentication" — fires when default_accounts_removed_or_changed is false, the default-credential foothold this rule covers (mapped to ATT&CK T1078.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: List broker users and confirm no shipped default account (RabbitMQ 'guest') remains with its default credentials.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: should NOT list 'guest' (deleted) — if present, verify it is loopback-restricted

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm any surviving guest user is loopback-only so the default account cannot authenticate remotely.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: loopback_users = guest (secure: guest is loopback-only) — 'loopback_users = none' is INSECURE (guest can connect remotely)

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Kafka/ActiveMQ deployments (no RabbitMQ guest account), confirm with the operator that no vendor-default principal or sample credential remains provisioned in the broker's identity store.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: no shipped default/sample principals usable; all accounts are deployment-provisioned

option_description: Whether the RabbitMQ built-in 'guest' user is present with its default password AND not restricted to loopback (loopback_users = none), so guest:guest can connect from remote networks.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Default / anonymous / weak broker authentication" — fires when default_guest_remotely_reachable is true, the remote default-credential path this rule covers (ATT&CK T1078.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read loopback_users to determine whether guest is confined to loopback or remotely reachable.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: loopback_users = guest (secure: guest is loopback-only) — 'loopback_users = none' is INSECURE (guest can connect remotely)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm whether the guest user still exists at all (deletion makes remote reachability moot).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: should NOT list 'guest' (deleted) — if present, verify it is loopback-restricted

option_description: Whether clients can connect without credentials — RabbitMQ advertising ANONYMOUS in auth_mechanisms, or a Kafka listener accepting unauthenticated connections.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Default / anonymous / weak broker authentication" — fires when anonymous_access_allowed is true, the no-credential connect path this rule covers (ATT&CK T1078.001 / T1071.005).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the RabbitMQ auth_mechanisms list for the ANONYMOUS SASL mechanism.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: auth_mechanisms.1 = PLAIN / .2 = AMQPLAIN (no ANONYMOUS) is secure; presence of ANONYMOUS is insecure

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Kafka, confirm no listener accepts unauthenticated connections (a reachable PLAINTEXT listener is unauthenticated).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SSL/SASL_SSL listeners (secure); a reachable PLAINTEXT://:9092 is insecure

option_description: Whether a Kafka authorizer is configured (authorizer.class.name set, e.g. StandardAuthorizer) so topic/group ACLs are actually enforced; false means no authorization at all.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Default / anonymous / weak broker authentication" — fires when kafka_authorizer_enabled is false (no authorization enforced). Not applicable to RabbitMQ/ActiveMQ (assess as true there).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check server.properties for an authorizer class and the default-ACL flag.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: StandardAuthorizer set + allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found = false (secure); true or missing authorizer is insecure (Confluent: production use of allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found strongly discouraged)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate ACLs to confirm the authorizer is live and enforcing per-principal rules.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: explicit per-principal/per-topic ACLs present; an empty ACL set combined with allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found=true means open access

option_description: The Kafka allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found flag — when true, any resource without an explicit ACL is world-accessible (default-allow), which Confluent discourages in production.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of TWO policy exposures: "Default / anonymous / weak broker authentication" and "Over-broad authorization / no per-topic least privilege" — both fire when kafka_allow_everyone_if_no_acl_found is true (default-allow on un-ACL'd resources).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the default-ACL flag in server.properties.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: StandardAuthorizer set + allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found = false (secure); true or missing authorizer is insecure (Confluent: production use of allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found strongly discouraged)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm explicit ACLs exist so that a true default-allow flag is not silently granting access to un-ACL'd resources.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: explicit per-principal/per-topic ACLs present; an empty ACL set combined with allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found=true means open access

option_description: Whether broker principals are scoped to least-privilege rights — RabbitMQ per-vhost configure/write/read regexes scoped per role, Kafka explicit per-principal/per-topic ACLs rather than super-user or default-allow.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Over-broad authorization / no per-topic least privilege" — fires when least_privilege_access_enforced is false (broad/wildcard rights, confused-deputy risk; ATT&CK T1071.005).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect per-vhost permission regexes for each RabbitMQ user; producers should be write-only, consumers read-only, not '.*' on all three.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: scoped regexes per vhost (secure) vs '.*' across vhosts (over-privileged)

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Kafka, list ACLs and confirm principals hold scoped per-topic rights rather than super-user grants.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: explicit per-principal/per-topic ACLs present; an empty ACL set combined with allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found=true means open access

option_description: Whether any application principal is granted wildcard authorization — RabbitMQ configure/write/read all '.*', or Kafka resource/operation wildcards / super-user-equivalent grants. An interpreted boolean read from the raw permission regexes / ACL list.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Over-broad authorization / no per-topic least privilege" — fires when wildcard_acls_used is true (a non-admin principal effectively holds all-resource rights; ATT&CK T1071.005).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the raw per-vhost permission regexes across users; '.*  .*  .*' for an application user is wildcard full access.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: per-user configure/write/read regexes — '.*  .*  .*' for an application user indicates wildcard full access (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: List Kafka ACLs and interpret whether any non-admin principal holds wildcard/all-resource rights.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: explicit per-principal/per-topic ACLs present; an empty ACL set combined with allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found=true means open access

option_description: Whether per-topic/per-queue authorization is actually enforced — Kafka authorizer set with allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found=false AND explicit ACLs; RabbitMQ scoped per-vhost permissions rather than a flat broad grant.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Over-broad authorization / no per-topic least privilege" — fires when per_topic_acls_enforced is false (no per-topic least-privilege boundary; ATT&CK T1071.005).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm an authorizer is active with deny-by-default in server.properties.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: StandardAuthorizer set + allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found = false (secure); true or missing authorizer is insecure (Confluent: production use of allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found strongly discouraged)

how_to_obtain.instruction: For RabbitMQ, confirm scoped per-vhost permissions per principal rather than a single broad grant.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: scoped regexes per vhost (secure) vs '.*' across vhosts (over-privileged)

option_description: Whether broker transport (AMQP, Kafka client and inter-broker channels) runs over TLS rather than cleartext, vs a reachable plaintext listener (AMQP 5672 / Kafka PLAINTEXT 9092 / inter-broker PLAINTEXT).
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Cleartext transport interception / MITM" — fires when flow_tls_encrypted is false (credentials/payloads exposed to sniffing/MITM; ATT&CK T1040 / T1557 / T1048.003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify a RabbitMQ TLS (AMQPS 5671) listener is configured with verify_peer.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: listeners.ssl.default = 5671, ssl_options.verify = verify_peer, ssl_options.versions.1 = tlsv1.3 (secure); verify_none or no TLS listener is insecure

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Kafka, confirm listeners use SSL/SASL_SSL rather than a reachable PLAINTEXT listener.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SSL/SASL_SSL listeners (secure); a reachable PLAINTEXT://:9092 is insecure

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm Kafka inter-broker replication is also encrypted.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SSL / SASL_SSL (secure) vs PLAINTEXT (insecure)

option_description: Whether the broker accepts ONLY TLS-protected connections, with no externally reachable cleartext listener remaining alongside the TLS one (the downgrade surface).
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Cleartext transport interception / MITM" — fires when tls_only_transport is false (a reachable plaintext port allows downgrade onto cleartext; ATT&CK T1040 / T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe the broker host: confirm the AMQPS port handshakes and that no plaintext port is reachable from untrusted networks.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: successful TLS 1.3 handshake on AMQPS; a refused/plaintext 5672 should be the only reachable port from untrusted networks

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate listening ports and confirm any plaintext port (5672 / Kafka 9092) is firewalled or not bound on the reachable interface.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ports bound to 127.0.0.1 or a private address, not 0.0.0.0; verify management.tcp.port is not publicly routable

option_description: Whether the broker's TLS listener still permits legacy TLS (TLSv1.0/1.1) in addition to/instead of TLSv1.2/1.3 — an interpreted flag from the negotiable protocol set (RabbitMQ ssl_options.versions, Kafka ssl.enabled.protocols).
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Cleartext transport interception / MITM" — fires when weak_tls_versions_enabled is true (legacy TLS enables downgrade/MITM; ATT&CK T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the RabbitMQ negotiable TLS protocol versions.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: listeners.ssl.default = 5671, ssl_options.verify = verify_peer, ssl_options.versions.1 = tlsv1.3 (secure); verify_none or no TLS listener is insecure

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the Kafka enabled protocol set.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TLSv1.2/TLSv1.3 only with keystore/truststore paths set (secure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: On the wire, enumerate negotiable protocols/ciphers on the TLS listener.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: only TLS 1.2/1.3 with strong (A-grade) ciphers; TLS 1.0/1.1 or weak ciphers indicate a weak listener

option_description: Whether peer/certificate verification is enforced on the TLS connection (RabbitMQ ssl_options.verify = verify_peer; Kafka clients validate the broker via a configured truststore), vs verify_none accepting any presented certificate.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Cleartext transport interception / MITM" — fires when server_certificate_validated is false (verify_none allows a forged-cert MITM even with TLS nominally on; ATT&CK T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the RabbitMQ peer-verification setting.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: listeners.ssl.default = 5671, ssl_options.verify = verify_peer, ssl_options.versions.1 = tlsv1.3 (secure); verify_none or no TLS listener is insecure

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Kafka, confirm a truststore is configured so clients validate the broker certificate chain.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TLSv1.2/TLSv1.3 only with keystore/truststore paths set (secure)

option_description: Whether mutual TLS is enforced so the broker requires a client certificate and rejects certless/anonymous TLS clients (RabbitMQ ssl_options.fail_if_no_peer_cert = true with verify_peer; Kafka ssl.client.auth = required).
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Cleartext transport interception / MITM" — fires when service_to_service_mtls_enforced is false (certless peers connect, weakening impersonation/MITM resistance; ATT&CK T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the RabbitMQ peer-cert requirement for mTLS.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ssl_options.fail_if_no_peer_cert = true (secure mTLS) vs false (accepts certless clients)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the Kafka client-auth mode.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: required (secure mTLS); none/requested are weaker per Confluent guidance

option_description: Whether the broker's data/messaging listeners (AMQP 5672/5671, Kafka 9092/9093, ActiveMQ OpenWire 61616) are bound to a publicly routable interface (0.0.0.0) and reachable from the internet rather than confined to a private/management network.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Internet-exposed broker / management plane" — fires when data_store_publicly_routable is true (direct surface for credential abuse and known-CVE exploitation; ATT&CK T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate listening sockets and confirm messaging ports are bound to a private/loopback address, not 0.0.0.0.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ports bound to 127.0.0.1 or a private address, not 0.0.0.0; verify management.tcp.port is not publicly routable

how_to_obtain.instruction: From an untrusted network, probe the broker's data ports to confirm they are not internet-reachable.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ports filtered/closed from the internet; only reachable from the private/management network

option_description: Whether the broker's administrative management plane — RabbitMQ management plugin HTTP API/UI on 15672 (15671 TLS) or an equivalent admin console — is listening on 0.0.0.0 and reachable from the internet.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Internet-exposed broker / management plane" — fires when management_ui_internet_exposed is true (a high-value admin-takeover surface; ATT&CK T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the management port binding (15672/15671) is on a private interface, not publicly routable.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ports bound to 127.0.0.1 or a private address, not 0.0.0.0; verify management.tcp.port is not publicly routable

how_to_obtain.instruction: From an untrusted network, attempt to reach the management UI/API to confirm it is firewalled off the internet.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: connection refused/timed out from the internet; the management UI is reachable only from trusted CIDRs

option_description: Whether network segmentation confines the broker so it accepts connections only from a management/trusted network, enforced in both broker config and network policy / firewall / security group.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Internet-exposed broker / management plane" — fires when segment_boundary_enforced is false (no segmentation isolates exposed listeners from untrusted networks; ATT&CK T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm broker listeners are bound to private interfaces as the broker-config half of the boundary.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ports bound to 127.0.0.1 or a private address, not 0.0.0.0; verify management.tcp.port is not publicly routable

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the firewall / security-group / network-policy rules confining the broker to the management/trusted network (the network-policy half of the boundary).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ingress to broker ports restricted to trusted CIDRs/SGs; no allow-all rule reaches messaging or management ports

option_description: Whether the broker's control-plane / admin API surface (RabbitMQ HTTP management API, Kafka admin/inter-node control on 25672, ActiveMQ console) is confined to a private/management network rather than publicly exposed.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Internet-exposed broker / management plane" — fires when control_plane_api_not_publicly_exposed is false (public control-plane API is a direct administrative surface; ATT&CK T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the HTTP management API and inter-node port (25672) are bound to private interfaces.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ports bound to 127.0.0.1 or a private address, not 0.0.0.0; verify management.tcp.port is not publicly routable

how_to_obtain.instruction: From an untrusted network, probe the control-plane endpoints (management API, inter-node 25672, ActiveMQ console) to confirm they are unreachable.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: control-plane ports filtered/closed from the internet; reachable only from the private/management network

option_description: Whether messages carry per-message integrity protection (application-layer digital signature or MAC over the body). Brokers do not sign bodies natively, so producers must sign and consumers verify before acting.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Message tampering / malicious injection" — fires when message_integrity_protected is false (forged/altered messages indistinguishable from legitimate traffic; ATT&CK T1659 / T1565.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the producer/consumer application design: confirm producers attach a signature/MAC over the message body and consumers verify it before processing. Brokers do not provide this natively.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: documented signing/verification (e.g. HMAC or detached signature over the payload) in the producer and consumer code paths

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect a sample message envelope to confirm an integrity header (signature/MAC) is present and validated.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: messages carry a verifiable integrity tag; consumers reject messages whose tag fails verification

option_description: Whether the broker requires authenticated producers before accepting a publish — no anonymous/guest write path (RabbitMQ guest deleted/loopback-only and ANONYMOUS removed; Kafka no reachable PLAINTEXT listener and an authorizer configured).
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Message tampering / malicious injection" — fires when producer_authentication_required is false (unauthenticated injection into a queue/topic; ATT&CK T1659 / T1565.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm there is no anonymous RabbitMQ write path: guest deleted or loopback-only.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: should NOT list 'guest' (deleted) — if present, verify it is loopback-restricted

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm ANONYMOUS is not advertised in RabbitMQ auth_mechanisms.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: auth_mechanisms.1 = PLAIN / .2 = AMQPLAIN (no ANONYMOUS) is secure; presence of ANONYMOUS is insecure

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Kafka, confirm no reachable PLAINTEXT listener offers an unauthenticated publish route.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SSL/SASL_SSL listeners (secure); a reachable PLAINTEXT://:9092 is insecure

option_description: Whether application principals hold wildcard/full publish authorization rather than scoped least-privilege write access — RabbitMQ write regex '.*', or Kafka allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found=true / no authorizer. An interpreted boolean over the real authorization config.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Message tampering / malicious injection" — fires when wildcard_publish_authorization is true (any authenticated principal can write to any queue/topic, enabling forged-message injection; ATT&CK T1659 / T1565.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read RabbitMQ write-permission regexes per principal; a write regex of '.*' is full publish authorization.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: scoped regexes per vhost (secure) vs '.*' across vhosts (over-privileged)

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Kafka, confirm an authorizer is set with deny-by-default so write access is not implicitly wildcard.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: StandardAuthorizer set + allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found = false (secure); true or missing authorizer is insecure (Confluent: production use of allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found strongly discouraged)

option_description: Whether message consumers enforce idempotency or deduplication (dedup on a unique key, Kafka enable.idempotence/transactional producers, or an application-side processed-id store) so re-delivering a previously processed message produces no duplicate side-effect.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Message replay" — fires when consumer_idempotency_or_dedup_enforced is false (a captured message can be replayed for duplicate side-effects such as repeated payments).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the consumer application: confirm it deduplicates on a unique message/business key or maintains a processed-id store so reprocessing is a no-op. The broker does not provide this natively.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: documented dedup/idempotency on a unique key, or Kafka enable.idempotence / transactional producers, with re-delivery producing no duplicate side-effect

how_to_obtain.instruction: Where Kafka producers are used, check for idempotent/transactional producer settings.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: enable.idempotence=true and/or a transactional.id set on producers

option_description: Whether messages carry an anti-replay binding the consumer validates — a per-message nonce, monotonic sequence number, or signed timestamp enforced against a freshness/acceptance window — so a stale captured message is rejected on resubmission.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Message replay" — fires when message_freshness_nonce_bound is false (previously captured messages remain indefinitely re-playable).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the message protocol/application design: confirm messages carry a nonce/sequence/signed-timestamp the consumer validates against a freshness window. Verified at the application layer, not a broker knob.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: documented anti-replay binding (nonce/sequence/signed-timestamp) with consumer-side freshness-window enforcement

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect a sample message envelope and confirm the freshness field is present and that resubmission of a stale message is rejected.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: stale/replayed messages rejected by the consumer; live messages within the window accepted

option_description: Whether the broker's persisted message store (Kafka log.dirs segments, RabbitMQ mnesia/quorum-queue data) sits on a volume encrypted at rest (LUKS or cloud KMS/EBS, AES-256). Brokers do not encrypt bodies natively.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Sensitive payloads unencrypted at rest / unbounded retention" — fires when encrypted_at_rest is false (cleartext PII/secrets persist on unencrypted disk).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the volume backing the broker data directory is encrypted (LUKS on-host or cloud-encrypted).
how_to_obtain.command: lsblk -o NAME,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT | grep -iE 'crypt|luks'  # or cloud: aws ec2 describe-volumes --query 'Volumes[].Encrypted'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: the volume backing log.dirs / RABBITMQ_MNESIA_BASE is crypt/LUKS or cloud-Encrypted=true

option_description: Whether messages carry a bounded TTL/retention so sensitive payloads are not retained indefinitely (Kafka retention.ms/retention.bytes finite, not -1; RabbitMQ x-message-ttl / message-ttl policy).
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Sensitive payloads unencrypted at rest / unbounded retention" — fires when retention_schedule_enforced is false (unbounded retention lets cleartext PII/secrets accumulate and leak into backups).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the per-topic retention settings on Kafka (or the message-ttl policy on RabbitMQ).
how_to_obtain.command: kafka-configs --bootstrap-server localhost:9093 --describe --entity-type topics --entity-name <topic>  # check retention.ms / retention.bytes
how_to_obtain.expected_output: a finite retention.ms (not -1/unbounded); for RabbitMQ check message-ttl policy via 'rabbitmqctl list_policies'

how_to_obtain.instruction: For RabbitMQ, confirm a message-ttl policy exists bounding queue message lifetime.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: a message-ttl (or max-length) policy is present, bounding retention; absence means unbounded

option_description: Whether sensitive message payload fields (PII, credentials, tokens) are masked/redacted before message bodies are written to broker logs or persisted diagnostics.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Sensitive payloads unencrypted at rest / unbounded retention" — fires when secrets_masked_in_logs is false (payloads leak verbatim into local logs, compounding the at-rest exposure).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect broker logs / diagnostics for any message-body content; confirm sensitive fields appear masked rather than verbatim.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: no cleartext PII/credentials/tokens in log lines; sensitive fields redacted (e.g. ****)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the logging configuration / application logging policy to confirm message-body logging is disabled or routed through a redaction layer.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: documented redaction/masking of payload fields before any body is logged

option_description: Whether a per-queue maximum length / overflow bound is enforced (RabbitMQ max-length / x-max-length-bytes / overflow policy with a dead-letter exchange, or Kafka per-topic retention.bytes) so an unbounded queue cannot exhaust memory/disk.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Queue flooding / resource-exhaustion DoS" — fires when queue_length_limit_enforced is false (a flood grows the queue until resources are exhausted; ATT&CK T1499.001 / T1499.003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check RabbitMQ policies for a max-length / overflow bound.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: a max-length / x-max-length-bytes policy with overflow + dead-letter present; absence means unbounded (firing)

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Kafka, confirm a finite per-topic retention.bytes caps the on-disk backlog.
how_to_obtain.command: kafka-configs --bootstrap-server localhost:9093 --describe --entity-type topics --entity-name <topic>  # check retention.ms / retention.bytes
how_to_obtain.expected_output: a finite retention.ms (not -1/unbounded); for RabbitMQ check message-ttl policy via 'rabbitmqctl list_policies'

option_description: Whether broker memory/disk safety watermarks are configured to back-pressure or block publishers before resources are exhausted (RabbitMQ vm_memory_high_watermark and disk_free_limit; Kafka retention/quota equivalents).
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Queue flooding / resource-exhaustion DoS" — fires when memory_disk_watermark_configured is false (a flood drives OOM / disk-full; ATT&CK T1499.001 / T1499.003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the RabbitMQ memory/disk watermark knobs.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E 'vm_memory_high_watermark|disk_free_limit' rabbitmq.conf  # plus 'rabbitmqctl list_policies' for max-length
how_to_obtain.expected_output: vm_memory_high_watermark and disk_free_limit set; queues have max-length / overflow policy and a dead-letter exchange

option_description: Whether per-client connection/publish rate limiting or producer quotas are enforced (RabbitMQ per-connection/channel limits and credit flow, Kafka client producer quotas) so a single principal cannot saturate the broker.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Queue flooding / resource-exhaustion DoS" — fires when rate_limiting_or_lockout_enabled is false (an abusive/compromised producer issues unbounded connections/messages; ATT&CK T1499.001 / T1499.003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check RabbitMQ for per-connection/channel limits bounding a single client's resource use.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E 'vm_memory_high_watermark|disk_free_limit' rabbitmq.conf  # plus 'rabbitmqctl list_policies' for max-length
how_to_obtain.expected_output: vm_memory_high_watermark and disk_free_limit set; queues have max-length / overflow policy and a dead-letter exchange

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Kafka, list configured client/producer quotas.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: per-client producer/consumer byte-rate quotas configured; no quotas means a single principal can saturate the broker

option_description: Whether network/connection-level flood protection guards the broker's reachable listeners (connection limits, SYN/connection rate caps, upstream load-balancer or WAF/scrubbing, IP-based throttling).
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Queue flooding / resource-exhaustion DoS" — fires when ddos_protection_in_place is false (listeners directly exposed to flooding with no protective layer; ATT&CK T1499.001 / T1499.003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the network architecture for a protective layer in front of the broker's listeners (LB/scrubbing/WAF, connection or SYN rate caps, IP throttling).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: documented connection/SYN rate caps or upstream LB/scrubbing absorbing floods before they reach broker queues

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect host/firewall connection-rate controls in front of the broker ports.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: connection/rate-limit rules present on the broker's listener ports; none means no host-level flood protection

option_description: Whether the broker software is running a release affected by a known, publicly-exploited RCE CVE (e.g. ActiveMQ OpenWire deserialization RCE CVE-2023-46604, fixed in ActiveMQ Classic >= 5.15.16/5.16.7/5.17.6/5.18.3 or Artemis >= 2.31.2).
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Unpatched broker RCE (ActiveMQ OpenWire)" — fires when unpatched_known_rce_cve is true (the running build is below the advisory fixed release; ATT&CK T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the deployed broker version and compare against the advisory fixed releases.
how_to_obtain.command: activemq --version   # or check the deployed broker package/image tag
how_to_obtain.expected_output: a patched version per the advisory; older builds are exploitable and likely internet-exposed if 61616/OpenWire is reachable

option_description: Whether the network-reachable broker software is kept current with security patches within the organisation's remediation SLA.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Unpatched broker RCE (ActiveMQ OpenWire)" — fires when edge_appliance_patched_within_sla is false (the broker is behind on security updates and exposed to known-CVE exploitation; ATT&CK T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the deployed broker version and check it against the patch SLA / latest advisory-fixed release.
how_to_obtain.command: activemq --version   # or check the deployed broker package/image tag
how_to_obtain.expected_output: a patched version per the advisory; older builds are exploitable and likely internet-exposed if 61616/OpenWire is reachable

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the patch-management record for the broker to confirm security updates are applied within the documented remediation SLA.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: broker patch dates fall within the org's remediation SLA; no overdue advisories outstanding

option_description: Whether the broker transport (e.g. ActiveMQ's OpenWire marshaller) deserializes attacker-influenced serialized class types from untrusted/unauthenticated network clients without a class allow-list.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "Unpatched broker RCE (ActiveMQ OpenWire)" — fires when native_deserialization_of_untrusted_data is true (an unrestricted deserialization sink is reachable, enabling arbitrary-class instantiation / shell execution; ATT&CK T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Determine the broker version (a patched OpenWire build constrains the deserialization sink) and whether the OpenWire transport is reachable.
how_to_obtain.command: activemq --version   # or check the deployed broker package/image tag
how_to_obtain.expected_output: a patched version per the advisory; older builds are exploitable and likely internet-exposed if 61616/OpenWire is reachable

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the transport config for a deserialization class allow-list and whether OpenWire is exposed to untrusted/unauthenticated peers.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: a restrictive serialization allow-list is set, or the transport is not reachable by untrusted peers; an unrestricted sink open to untrusted clients is the firing state

option_description: Whether the broker records an access/authentication audit trail (connection and auth attempts on AMQP/Kafka listeners) — RabbitMQ auth/connection event logging; Kafka authorizer.logger.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "No audit logging of connections / publish-consume / admin events" — fires when access_audit_trail_enabled is false (anonymous access and credential abuse become undetectable; ATT&CK T1562.008).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the broker logging config for auth/connection (RabbitMQ) or authorizer (Kafka) logging.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E 'log.level|log.file|authorizer.logger' server.properties  # Kafka; RabbitMQ: grep 'log.' rabbitmq.conf
how_to_obtain.expected_output: authorizer logging enabled and logs forwarded off-box; verify a SIEM/forwarder consumes broker logs
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 - Audit Log Management

option_description: Whether all security-relevant broker events are captured — including publish/consume operations and authorization (ACL) decisions, not just startup/error logs (Kafka authorizer logger; RabbitMQ auth/connection events).
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "No audit logging of connections / publish-consume / admin events" — fires when security_events_fully_logged is false (tampering and publish/consume abuse leave no forensic trail; ATT&CK T1562.008).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the authorizer/ACL-decision logger and connection logging are enabled (not just error/startup logs).
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E 'log.level|log.file|authorizer.logger' server.properties  # Kafka; RabbitMQ: grep 'log.' rabbitmq.conf
how_to_obtain.expected_output: authorizer logging enabled and logs forwarded off-box; verify a SIEM/forwarder consumes broker logs
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 - Audit Log Management

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the broker log stream to confirm publish/consume and ACL-decision events actually appear.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: log entries for authorization decisions and publish/consume operations are present, not only startup/error lines

option_description: Whether broker logs are shipped off-box to a separate system / SIEM rather than retained only on the broker host.
security_impact: One of the OR-conditions of the policy exposure "No audit logging of connections / publish-consume / admin events" — fires when logs_stored_on_separate_system is false (an attacker who compromises the broker can erase the trail; ATT&CK T1562.008).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a forwarder/SIEM pipeline ships broker logs off-box rather than local-only retention.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E 'log.level|log.file|authorizer.logger' server.properties  # Kafka; RabbitMQ: grep 'log.' rabbitmq.conf
how_to_obtain.expected_output: authorizer logging enabled and logs forwarded off-box; verify a SIEM/forwarder consumes broker logs
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 - Audit Log Management

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm with operations that broker logs are received and retained in a separate SIEM/log store independent of the broker host.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: broker log events visible in the SIEM with adequate retention; not solely on the broker host

option_description: Whether broker administrative changes are audited — RabbitMQ vhost/user/permission (ACL) changes via rabbitmqctl, Kafka ACL/super.users/topic-config changes.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm admin/ACL-change events are captured by the broker logging configuration.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E 'log.level|log.file|authorizer.logger' server.properties  # Kafka; RabbitMQ: grep 'log.' rabbitmq.conf
how_to_obtain.expected_output: authorizer logging enabled and logs forwarded off-box; verify a SIEM/forwarder consumes broker logs
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 - Audit Log Management

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect logs for administrative-change events (vhost/user/permission changes on RabbitMQ; ACL/super.users/topic-config changes on Kafka).
